annotations.description: The player chose to mulligan a very keepable 7-card hand. The hand has 5 lands (4 Swamps + Thriving Moor), Devouring Swarm (a solid 3-drop), and Skullslither Worm (a strong 4-drop). While the hand is land-heavy, it has a clean curve of turn 3 Devouring Swarm into turn 4 Skullslither Worm (which forces a discard). The Thriving Moor can even choose green if needed for later splashes. Going to 6 cards means losing a card for no good reason — this hand functions perfectly well and has two quality spells on curve. Land-heavy hands are much better than land-light hands, and mulliganing to 6 in limited is a significant cost.
annotations.actionTaken: Mulliganed a 7-card hand with 5 lands, Devouring Swarm, and Skullslither Worm.
annotations.betterLine: Keep the 7-card hand. Play Devouring Swarm on turn 3, Skullslither Worm on turn 4, and draw into more spells with the extra card.

annotations.description: Put the only land in hand (Thriving Moor) on the bottom of the library, leaving a 5-card hand with zero lands. All spells in hand cost 2+ mana, with most costing 3-5 mana. With no lands, the player cannot cast anything and must draw multiple lands before becoming functional, which is devastating after already mulliganing to 5.
annotations.actionTaken: Put Thriving Moor on the bottom, keeping a zero-land hand of all spells.
annotations.betterLine: Bottom Rise Again (expensive, situational 5-mana sorcery that needs a creature in graveyard) or Grotesque Mutation (reactive combat trick) instead, keeping the only land to have a chance at curving out.

annotations.description: Bottomed a Swamp instead of Massacre Wurm, leaving only 2 lands in a 5-card hand. While Massacre Wurm is powerful, at 6 mana (3BBB) it's extremely expensive and the player needs to draw multiple lands in a row just to cast their 3-drop on time. A 2-land, 5-card hand is very risky in Limited.
annotations.actionTaken: Bottomed a Swamp, keeping a 2-land hand with Massacre Wurm (6 mana)
annotations.betterLine: Bottom Massacre Wurm to keep 3 Swamps, ensuring on-curve Liliana's Devotee on turn 3 and Strangling Spores on turn 4. Massacre Wurm is too expensive to justify keeping in a mana-light mulligan hand.

annotations.description: Playing Forest instead of Thriving Heath on turn 1 when there's no 1-mana play available. The tapped land should be played when the tempo cost is free (turn 1 with no 1-drop). Both lines work for the curve, but playing Heath now choosing green would give flexible mana while 'wasting' the enters-tapped downside on a turn where no mana is needed.
annotations.betterLine: Play Thriving Heath (choosing green) turn 1, taking advantage of having no 1-drop to absorb the enters-tapped tempo loss for free

annotations.description: Playing Plains instead of Thriving Heath on a turn where neither enables a cast. Thriving Heath enters tapped, making this the ideal turn to play it (no spells castable with 3 mana anyway). Saving Plains for a later turn when entering untapped matters is better sequencing. Additionally, Thriving Heath (choosing green) provides more color flexibility than Plains.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Plains (enters untapped but can't use the mana productively this turn)
annotations.betterLine: Play Thriving Heath (choosing green) now while you can't cast anything anyway, saving Plains for a turn where entering untapped enables an on-curve play

annotations.description: Failed to attack with 2/2 Ironshell Beetle when the opponent has no untapped creatures to block (Black Cat is summoning sick) and no untapped lands to cast tricks. This is 2 free damage with zero risk.
annotations.actionTaken: Timed out and did not declare any attackers.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with Ironshell Beetle for 2 unblocked damage.

annotations.description: Thriving Heath entered the battlefield and the player timed out on the color choice, likely defaulting to Blue instead of choosing Green. With a G/W deck and multiple green cards in hand (Moldgraf Millipede, Nantuko Cultivator, Thriving Grove), choosing Green would have given the Heath flexibility to produce either W or G, smoothing mana significantly. Blue is useless for this deck.
annotations.actionTaken: Timed out on Thriving Heath color choice, defaulting to a likely useless color (Blue)
annotations.betterLine: Choose Green for Thriving Heath to maximize mana flexibility for the G/W deck, enabling easier casting of green-heavy spells like Moldgraf Millipede and Nantuko Cultivator

annotations.description: Failed to attack with Ironshell Beetle 2/2 when the opponent had no available blockers (Liliana's Devotee is summoning sick). This was 2 free, uncontested damage that was missed due to timeout.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with Ironshell Beetle 2/2 for 2 unblockable damage, putting opponent to 18.

This is a free favorable block that also triggers Devotee's 'creature died this turn' ability for potential zombie token creation. Instead, MiniMx timed out and took 2 unnecessary damage while leaving the opponent's creature alive.

annotations.betterLine: Block Ironshell Beetle with Liliana's Devotee. Devotee survives at 1 toughness remaining, Beetle dies, and the creature death enables Devotee's end step zombie token ability.

annotations.description: Attempted to cast Eaten Alive without being able to pay the additional cost ({3}{B} requires 5 mana, only 3 available). Sacrificing Ghoulraiser or Liliana's Devotee to remove a 2/2 Knight would also be a poor trade. The game rolled back the action.

annotations.betterLine: Cast Black Cat for {1}{B} - it deploys a useful body that can later be sacrificed to Eaten Alive as the additional cost, and preserves the more valuable creatures on board.

annotations.description: Failed to declare any attackers with two vigilance creatures (Gallant Cavalry 2/2 and Knight Token 2/2). Since both have vigilance, attacking has no defensive downside — they remain untapped for blocking. The opponent would need to either take damage or make blocking decisions with Ghoulraiser and Liliana's Devotee. At minimum, attacking forces the opponent into uncomfortable choices and potentially deals 2-4 damage for free.
annotations.actionTaken: Timed out and declared no attackers.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with both vigilance creatures. Opponent either takes 4 damage or must block, and the attackers remain untapped for defense regardless.

annotations.description: Failed to assign any blockers against two 2/2 attackers, taking 4 unnecessary damage. Liliana's Devotee (2/3) could block and kill a 2/2 while surviving, and Black Cat could chump the other (dying to trigger random discard from opponent's 2-card hand and enabling Devotee's end-step zombie token). This would result in 0 damage taken, both attackers killed, Devotee surviving, a forced discard, and a free zombie token.
annotations.actionTaken: Timed out with no blockers assigned, taking 4 damage.
annotations.betterLine: Block one 2/2 with Liliana's Devotee (survives, kills attacker) and the other with Black Cat (dies, forces random discard, enables Devotee zombie trigger). Take 0 damage, kill both attackers, gain a zombie token.

annotations.description: Failed to declare any attackers when the opponent had only one untapped blocker (Liliana's Devotee 2/3) and all lands tapped (no tricks possible). Attacking with all three creatures would deal 4-10 damage depending on blocks, with the vigilance creatures staying untapped for defense. The Moldgraf Millipede at 6/6 is a massive threat that demands a block, letting the two vigilance 2/2s through for guaranteed damage.
annotations.actionTaken: Timed out and declared no attackers, dealing 0 damage.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with all three creatures (Moldgraf Millipede 6/6, Gallant Cavalry 2/2 vigilance, Knight Token 2/2 vigilance). This forces the opponent to either take 10 damage or block one creature and still take 4-8 damage, likely killing their Devotee in the process.

annotations.description: Failed to declare any blockers against 10 total damage (2/2 + 2/2 + 6/6). Liliana's Devotee (2/3) could safely block and kill a 2/2, and the Zombie Token (3/2) could chump-block the 6/6 Millipede. This would reduce damage taken from 10 to just 2, keeping life at 14 instead of dropping to 6. The Zombie Token dying would also trigger Devotee's end-step zombie creation. Going to 6 life with the opponent having this board is extremely dangerous.
annotations.actionTaken: No blocks declared (timeout/no response), taking 10 damage to go to 6 life.
annotations.betterLine: Block Gallant Cavalry (or Knight Token) with Liliana's Devotee (kills the 2/2, Devotee survives at 2/1) and block Moldgraf Millipede with the Zombie Token (prevents 6 damage, token dies triggering Devotee's ability). Take only 2 damage, going to 14 life.

annotations.description: MiniMx declined to attack with Liliana's Devotee (2/3) and Zombie Token (3/2) into only two 2/2 vigilance creatures. In every scenario, attacking is superior: if blocked, both MiniMx creatures survive (3 toughness and 2 toughness vs 2 power) while killing the opponent's 2/2s, reducing next turn's incoming damage. If unblocked, 5 damage pushes the opponent from 18 toward a more manageable life total. Additionally, killing creatures triggers Liliana's Devotee end-step ability for a free zombie token. Not attacking preserves the opponent's board unnecessarily when MiniMx is behind at 6 life.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to attack with any creatures.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with both Liliana's Devotee and Zombie Token. They win every combat trade against the 2/2 vigilance blockers, clearing the opponent's board of those threats while MiniMx's creatures survive, and potentially triggering Devotee's end-step zombie creation.

annotations.description: Failed to play a Forest from hand when there was a land drop available and no reason not to. Playing the land is pure upside - it adds an extra mana source for future turns at zero cost. With an empty hand after playing it, there's no strategic reason to hold it.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without playing the Forest, missing the land drop.
annotations.betterLine: Play the Forest, then proceed to combat. The extra mana could matter in subsequent turns.

annotations.description: Player timed out and failed to declare any attackers with a dominant board (6/6, 3/4, two 2/2 vigilance creatures) against an opponent at 6 life with only two blockers and all lands tapped. Attacking all would force at least 4-5 damage through (opponent at 1-2 life) with minimal risk, since the vigilance creatures remain untapped for defense. This gives the opponent a free turn to stabilize, use Infernal Idol to draw cards, and potentially find answers like Massacre Wurm or Yargle.
annotations.actionTaken: No response — failed to declare any attackers, passing the combat phase entirely.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with all four creatures. Opponent can only block two, and any blocking configuration lets at least 4 damage through (likely 5), putting them to 1-2 life. With vigilance creatures still untapped for defense and a Forest in hand, this is an overwhelming attack with virtually no downside.

annotations.description: At 6 life facing 13 damage from four attackers, MiniMx timed out and declared no blockers, dying to the attack. Blocking Moldgraf Millipede (6/6) and Iridescent Hornbeetle (3/4) would have reduced incoming damage to 4, allowing survival at 2 life with Massacre Wurm in hand for next turn (which would wipe the opponent's small creatures).
annotations.actionTaken: No response (timeout) — no blockers declared, taking 13 lethal damage at 6 life.
annotations.betterLine: Block Moldgraf Millipede with Zombie Token and Iridescent Hornbeetle with Liliana's Devotee. Only 4 damage gets through, surviving at 2 life. Next turn, cast Massacre Wurm to give opponent's creatures -2/-2, killing the 2/2s and potentially stabilizing.
